identity.observed_title: SOUL FALL / THE LAST SIGNAL / BUILD 82
identity.note: Build number observed on title screen; source deliberately not inspected.

method.input: Helper JSON-lines native-CDP touch, at most two contacts; visible selectors and normalized geometry only
method.inspected: Only helper --help and own visible screenshots/UI output; no game source, tests, docs, prior reviews, recordings, internal state or target metadata inspected. Own evidence directory names listed for reporting.
method.capture_policy: Every returned screenshot viewed before adaptive input. Captures generally paused play for inspection; planning map remained open until visibly closed with #close-map. This substantially reduces uninterrupted pressure and does not assess continuous enjoyment.
method.renderer: Synthetic paused Chromium emulation with software-WebGL fallback; not certified physical-device experience

result.note: End UI labels time as cumulative play time. This was the only attempt; no retry. Last pre-loss capture showed 33 health, 22 shield, 30/251 ammunition at 00:45; terminal UI does not show health/ammunition.

not_exercised: map local zoom or manual target selection

observations.detail: Opening guard was centered and its optic was visually distinct. A roughly 2.5-second FIRE hold with a small upward drag cleared it without losing health or shield; terminal UI later confirmed one critical elimination.
Map showed a clear cyan walking route and receiver reach circles. Near Mara, visible prompt said 1.5 m outside reach; holding USE with a short northward movement then stopping recovered her.
Objective text, numbered memory chips and MEMORY RECOVERED SERA NORD banner confirmed progress. Health rose from 13 to 33 after this recovery, giving a welcome reprieve.
Strong stormy teal art direction, large title and prominent deployment button made the start clear at 390 px width.

At the archive exit, north/east movement and a jump attempt left a similar pillar/wall-obstructed view and the same 22 m map route. Health dropped from 100/22 shield to 70/0 and then 13/0 while I tried to escape. Cannot establish whether collision, my route execution or touch placement caused the failure.

Threat chevrons signaled damage, but enemies often remained outside the forward view. I spent attention on movement/map rather than acquiring them. A nearby enemy became visible on the left while I was at 13 health.
Backpedaled while firing and dragging aim left, then strafed right and tapped DASH. This changed the view and got clear enough to reach Sera; no phase evade was credited.

Firing while moving toward Sera exhausted the magazine without a visible kill. Reload restored 30 rounds. Final accuracy was only 4%; this reflects my attempt, not an isolated weapon accuracy measurement.

After Sera, attempted east/southeast movement for 4.5 seconds toward Elian. Follow-up map tap returned Selector must be visible because play had ended; the next capture visibly confirmed SIGNAL LOST. No retry or extra gameplay followed.

scores.scale: 0 unusable, 2 severe barriers, 5 workable with substantial friction, 7 good with noticeable issues, 9 excellent, 10 exceptional. Subjective scores limited to this single emulated attempt; overall is holistic, not a completion grade or arithmetic average.

controls.reason: Two-contact firing/movement, USE and map worked. Fine navigation around the archive was difficult; aim and movement under unseen fire demanded more coordination than I managed.

gameplay.reason: Immediate guard encounter and two recoveries provided clear progress and a recovery reprieve. Patrol pressure during navigation was punishing; late mission mechanics were not reached.

presentation.reason: Cohesive teal storm atmosphere, weapon and enemy silhouettes, strong title and loss-screen hierarchy. Audio and hardware rendering quality unassessed.

usability.reason: Compact handbook, explicit proximity guidance and paused route map helped. Needed repeated planning interruptions to navigate; dense controls and obstructed views made live decisions difficult.

readability.reason: Health, ammunition, objectives and action buttons were readable. Small map legend, secondary text and competing spatial markers required deliberate inspection at portrait width.

uncertainties: Navigation failure is an observed experience, not a confirmed collision defect.
Off-screen attackers and exact damage sources were not identified reliably.
Software rendering and capture pauses prevent conclusions about real phone performance, touch feel or sustained pacing.
Frozen hash supplied by user; no source inspection used to verify it.

cleanup.result: Exact owned driver and Chrome PIDs absent after helper exit; no kill commands used.
